title: Diet for a New America: How Your Food Choices Affect Your Health, Happiness and the Future of Life on Earth
author: John Robbins
target_audience: General readers curious about the effects of diet on society and environment
core_themes: The health impacts of dietary choices
Ethical and environmental consequences of animal agriculture
Plant-based diets as a path to personal and planetary health
Industrial food production and its hidden costs
The connection between diet, well-being, and ecological sustainability
primary_purpose: To educate readers on the profound impacts of diet—not only on personal health, but also on animal welfare and the global environment—and to advocate for a shift toward a plant-based diet as a path to wellness, compassion, and sustainability.

structure_format.narrative_style: Engaging, persuasive, and evidence-based with personal anecdotes
structure_format.organization: Divided into three main sections: the role of diet in health, the ethical issues surrounding animal agriculture, and the environmental impacts of food production
features: Actionable suggestions for changing dietary habits

key_concepts_lessons: A diet high in animal products is linked to increased risks of chronic diseases such as heart disease, cancer, and diabetes.
Animal agriculture contributes significantly to environmental degradation, including deforestation, water pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.
Industrialized farming practices often involve ethical concerns regarding animal suffering.
Shifting to a plant-based diet can improve personal health, reduce ecological impact, and promote a more compassionate society.
Consumers have the power to drive positive change through their food choices.
notable_features: Pioneering exploration of the intersections between diet, ethics, and ecology
Extensive use of research and data for argumentation
Call to action for readers to reconsider traditional eating patterns
Influential in the rise of plant-based and vegan movements in North America
cultural_historical_context: Published during the late 1980s, a period of growing awareness about health, environmental issues, and animal rights. Robbins, heir to the Baskin-Robbins ice cream fortune, used his personal background to underscore the importance of individual choice and responsibility in shaping a sustainable and humane food future.
reception_impact: Highly influential in the plant-based and vegan movements
Praised for its thorough research and passionate advocacy
Used as a foundational text in health, environmental, and ethical circles
Criticized by some for a perceived anti-meat bias and controversial health claims, though many points have been supported by subsequent research
comparable_titles: The China Study by T. Colin Campbell and Thomas M. Campbell
Fast Food Nation by Eric Schlosser
Eating Animals by Jonathan Safran Foer
